concepts.title: Work Done by a Force
concepts.body: Work is done when a force acts on an object and causes it to move in the direction of the force. The amount of work done depends on the magnitude of the force and the distance the object moves. For example, pushing a shopping cart across a store involves work because the force applied moves the cart forward.

concepts.title: Kinetic Energy and Potential Energy
concepts.body: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion, calculated as (1/2)mv^2. Potential energy is the energy stored in an object due to its position or height, calculated as mgh. For instance, a ball rolling down a hill has kinetic energy, while a book placed on a shelf has potential energy.

concepts.title: Law of Conservation of Energy
concepts.body: The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another. For example, when a pendulum swings, its potential energy converts to kinetic energy and vice versa, but the total energy remains constant.

formulas.title: Work Done
formulas.body: W = F x s (W in joule J, F in newton N, s in meter m). This formula calculates the work done when a force F moves an object by a distance s in the direction of the force.

formulas.title: Kinetic Energy and Potential Energy
formulas.body: Kinetic Energy = (1/2)mv^2 (KE in joule J, m in kg, v in m/s). Potential Energy = mgh (PE in joule J, m in kg, g in m/s^2, h in m). These formulas are used to calculate the kinetic energy of a moving object and the potential energy of an object at a height h.

examples.title: Everyday Example
examples.body: When you lift a bucket of water from the ground to a table, you do work against gravity. The force you apply moves the bucket upward, and the work done is calculated using W = F x s.

examples.title: Applied Example
examples.body: In a hydroelectric power plant, water stored at a height has potential energy. When it flows down, this energy converts to kinetic energy, which is then used to generate electricity.

mcqs.question: What is the unit of work?
mcqs.explanation: The unit of work is joule (J). Newton is the unit of force, watt is the unit of power, and pascal is the unit of pressure.

mcqs.question: A car of mass 1000 kg is moving at a speed of 20 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
mcqs.explanation: Kinetic energy is calculated as (1/2)mv^2. Substituting m = 1000 kg and v = 20 m/s, KE = (1/2) x 1000 x (20)^2 = 200,000 J. The other options are incorrect calculations.

mcqs.question: A ball is dropped from a height of 10 m. What is its potential energy just before it hits the ground? (g = 10 m/s^2)
mcqs.explanation: Potential energy is calculated as mgh. Just before hitting the ground, the height h is 0 m, so PE = m x g x 0 = 0 J. The other options are incorrect because they do not consider the height being zero.
